title: A GRAPH-BASED CLUSTERING AND LARGE LANGUAGE MODEL-ENHANCED ASPECT-BASED SENTIMENT ANALYSIS FRAMEWORK FOR MODELING PASSENGER SATISFACTION IN EUROPEAN CRUISE ITINERARIES
abstract: Cruise tourism offers travelers the opportunity to visit multiple destinations while enjoying various onboard services. It has emerged as one of the fastest growing sectors in the tourism industry. Online reviews have become an essential resource for both travelers and cruise operators, with the rapid increase in user-generated content on online platforms. This study presents a novel framework for analyzing cruise passenger satisfaction across European itineraries by integrating transitive clustering, topic modeling, and Aspect Based Sentiment Analysis (ABSA). Cruises were grouped into four major geographic regions based on the ports they visited. Eight key aspects from online reviews were identified where three of them are itinerary related. The GPT-4o mini large language model, accessed through the OpenAI API, was used for fine-grained sentence-level aspect-based sentiment analysis. Results show that cruises in the Eastern Mediterranean received the highest satisfaction scores across itinerary related aspects while those in the Western European and Atlantic Coastal scored lowest. This study highlights the effectiveness of the GPT-4o mini large language model in extracting nuanced sentiment from informal online reviews. It also identifies the most and least satisfying cruise regions in Europe based on customer feedback, while providing an aspect×region knowledge map for decision support.

title: Transpilation and optimization of QAOA for maximum weighted independent set
abstract: In recent years, quantum computing has shown promise in solving certain problems more efficiently than classical methods. The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) has emerged as a leading candidate for achieving quantum advantage on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices. This study explores the application of QAOA to the Maximum Weighted Independent Set (MWIS) problem, with particular focus on circuit transpilation strategies and parameter optimization methods. Using IBM Qiskit, we systematically examine factors affecting QAOA performance, including different transpilation optimization levels and classical optimizer selection. Our results demonstrate that optimization level 3 reduced circuit depth by 32% compared to level 0 for p=3 circuits, while maintaining solution quality. Among classical optimizers, COBYLA achieved an 81.24% approximation ratio with only 54.8 function evaluations at p=2, outperforming both grid search and SPSA methods. Execution on IBM’s real quantum hardware resulted in performance degradation ranging from 16% at p=1 to 34% at p=3 compared to ideal simulations, highlighting the compounding impact of noise and gate errors as circuit depth increases.These findings provide practical guidance for quantum algorithm implementation on NISQ devices, demonstrating that appropriate selection of transpilation techniques and optimization methods can substantially improve quantum resource efficiency while maintaining solution quality.

title: Synchronization Strings over the Optimal Alphabet
abstract: Synchronization strings provide deterministic position labels for recovering coordinates after insertions and deletions. Haeupler and Shahrasbi introduced these objects, and subsequent work proved that four symbols suffice for some fixed parameter epsilon < 1, whereas two symbols cannot support arbitrarily long synchronization strings. We resolve the remaining ternary case: every length admits a ternary 2001/2002-synchronization string. Thus three is the exact minimum constant alphabet size. A computer-assisted refinement based on a larger 54-uniform family yields ternary epsilon-synchronization strings for every epsilon > 215/216. The previous four-symbol construction uses a ternary square-free backbone to exclude short repetitions and a fourth symbol to carry long-range synchronization marks. Our main technical contribution is a local-entropy transfer theorem: every square-free block-local source with a positive interval conditional min-entropy rate supports synchronization strings with a fixed gap. We instantiate this theorem using occurrence-wise branching in a Brinkhuis family. Every outcome remains ternary and square-free, while every long interval retains linear conditional min-entropy after all choices outside it are exposed. A deletion-ball estimate converts this entropy into an exponentially small probability of a near-complete common subsequence between adjacent intervals, and an asymmetric Lovasz Local Lemma enforces all interval constraints simultaneously. The same framework also yields exponentially many valid words, synchronization circles, and synchronization within a class of extremal square-free words. Adding constraints on distant intervals gives a Las Vegas construction in expected O(n^2 log^3(n+2)) time.

title: SafeRI: Recognition and Intervention for Token-Level Safety Intervention in Large Vision Language Models
abstract: Existing safety alignment methods for vision-language models usually modify the model behavior globally: once the safety parameters are trained or loaded, they participate in both unsafe and already-safe generations. This always-on intervention can unnecessarily perturb the model's original reasoning path and degrade general multimodal capabilities. We argue that safety alignment should be an on-demand intervention rather than a permanent modification to every decoding trajectory. To this end, we propose a streaming recognition and gated LoRA framework for intrinsic VLM safety. During autoregressive generation, a lightweight recognizer estimates whether the current pre-token generation state is safe or unsafe. Its output updates the LoRA gate for the following decoding step; otherwise, generation follows the frozen-backbone policy. The LoRA module is trained from unsafe prefixes, transition statements, and safe continuations, so that it learns to redirect unsafe generations back to safe responses after activation. Experiments across multiple safety and general-purpose benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in post-alignment settings.

title: Introducing SINFONIA: Symplectic, slimplectic and Magnusian (Neural) Flows for Orbital Numerical Integration and Acceleration
abstract: Long-duration gravitational-wave modelling must resolve fast orbital motion together with slow dissipative evolution while preventing small numerical errors from accumulating into secular phase drift. Here we ask whether the finite-time evolution map itself can be learned as an explicit, differentiable, structure-preserving object and then repeatedly composed through a complete inspiral. We construct three neural-flow architectures: a symplectic and slimplectic flow on Galley's doubled phase space, [SINFONIA-J0]; a Taylor-anchored flow, [SINFONIA-J1]; and a Magnusian flow that learns the finite-time dissipative correction in the interaction picture, [SINFONIA-J2]. Applied to a 2.5PN neutron-star inspiral, all three expose the same controlling mechanism: long-time accuracy is governed not by pointwise map error alone, but by its signed projection onto a single secular channel fixed by energy--angular-momentum balance. Encoding this structure allows the learned maps to remain accurate through $10^{2}$--$10^{5}$ window compositions to coalescence at timesteps of a full orbital period and beyond, reaching chained phase errors orders of magnitude below a benchmark slimplectic integrator at lower cost. The same secular structure can also be exploited for physics inference: when the channel is left unconstrained, the accumulated phase retains enough information to recover an un-modelled dynamical-friction-like force, both parametrically and as a learned function of separation. Network-off controls isolate the contribution of learning from the analytic structure already built into each map. These results establish a proof of concept for structure-preserving learned evolution maps as tools for fast long-duration integration and physics inference in gravitational-wave source modelling.

title: Systematic Gap Analysis of Security Vulnerabilities in LLM Fine-Tuning
abstract: The recent rise in organisations fine-tuning their own large language models has created a multitude of new attack vectors for adversaries to exploit across domains such as healthcare, law, and finance. This new adaptation to stay future-proof has developed an under-studied landscape of adversarial vulnerabilities specific to the fine-tuning phase of large language models. This study provides a systematic literature review of the field, aiming to create a threat taxonomy and conduct a gap analysis. The final corpus of 82 academic papers revealed five main attack vectors: data poisoning, backdoor injection, malicious fine-tuning, instruction-tuning vulnerabilities, and reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) exploitation. The corresponding defences were classified into three broad categories: robust fine-tuning, backdoor removal and PEFT defence, and data poisoning defences. A comparison between attacks and defences revealed alarming gaps in research. Most literature focused on data poisoning and backdoor injections, with a disproportionately small amount dedicated to instruction-tuning vulnerabilities and RLHF exploitation. Furthermore, the defences for each attack category remained fragmented, with no standardised best-practice method emerging from the literature.

title: ALGORITMOS QUÂNTICOS: Da lógica clássica à computação quântica
abstract: Algoritmos Quânticos: Da lógica clássica à computação quântica apresenta uma introdução progressiva, técnica e computacional aos fundamentos e aos principais algoritmos da computação quântica. A obra parte dos conceitos clássicos de algoritmo, complexidade computacional, teoria dos números e álgebra linear para construir, passo a passo, a compreensão de qubits, superposição, medição, interferência, portas quânticas, circuitos e emaranhamento. Ao longo do livro são desenvolvidos algoritmos fundamentais como Deutsch, Deutsch–Jozsa, Simon e Grover, avançando para a Transformada Quântica de Fourier (QFT), estimação quântica de fase e o algoritmo de Shor. A obra também discute amplificação de amplitude, criptografia pós-quântica, computação híbrida quântico-clássica, VQE, QAOA, barren plateaus, ruído, correção e mitigação de erros, além dos diferentes significados de vantagem quântica e dos limites atuais da tecnologia. Uma parte substancial do livro é dedicada à implementação prática com Python e Qiskit, incluindo preparação e medição de estados, estados de Bell, circuitos de Grover, QFT, estimação de fase, demonstrações de Shor, simulação local, transpilação e execução em processadores quânticos (QPUs). O texto procura distinguir rigorosamente vantagem algorítmica teórica, vantagem experimental e utilidade prática, evitando interpretações excessivamente simplificadas da computação quântica. O objetivo é oferecer uma ponte entre Ciência da Computação clássica e computação quântica para estudantes, desenvolvedores, pesquisadores e leitores interessados em compreender não apenas como os algoritmos quânticos funcionam, mas também quando, por que e sob quais condições eles podem oferecer vantagens computacionais. title: Quantum Complexity Theory - Computational Landscape Analysis
abstract: Quantum Complexity Theory (QCT) represents a paradigm shift in our understanding of computational complexity, moving beyond classical approaches to explore the potential of quantum mechanics. This paper proposes a novel algorithm, the "Entangled Search Algorithm" (ESA), designed to analyze the computational landscape of a given problem, leveraging quantum entanglement to efficiently identify optimal solutions. We argue that this approach offers a significant advantage over existing methods, particularly in tackling complex problems with inherent quantum features. The ESA utilizes quantum entanglement to create a dynamic landscape of possibilities, enabling a more targeted and potentially faster search for solutions. This work details the fundamental concepts, algorithm implementation, and preliminary results demonstrating the potential of this approach.

title: Bayesian Constraint Optimization for Quantum State Collapse
abstract: Quantum state collapse is a fundamental process in quantum mechanics, and its optimization represents a significant challenge for practical quantum computing. This paper explores the application of Bayesian constraint optimization to this problem, proposing a novel framework that dynamically adjusts collapse probabilities based on observation and internal feedback loops. We move beyond traditional probability density calculations by constructing a Bayesian network to continuously refine the collapse strategy. This approach offers a path towards more efficient and robust quantum state control, addressing limitations of conventional methods and paving the way for enhanced quantum algorithm performance. The paper details the theoretical foundation, implementation of the Bayesian network, and preliminary results demonstrating the framework's effectiveness in a simplified quantum system.

title: Adaptive Topology Matrix for Machine Learning
abstract: This paper introduces an Adaptive Topology Matrix (ATM) for machine learning, designed to enhance model generalization, particularly in the face of high-dimensional data and non-standard data distributions. Traditional machine learning models often rely on static feature representations and parameters, struggling to effectively address complex data patterns. The ATM leverages an iterative self-adaptive optimization process, incorporating deep learning techniques to dynamically adjust the topology of the model. This approach significantly improves the model's ability to handle intricate data characteristics, leading to enhanced performance across a range of applications. The paper details the core mechanism, including the design of the adaptive self-adaptive optimization algorithm and the utilization of deep learning for feature representation learning. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the ATM through a series of simulations and experiments, showcasing its potential to boost generalization capabilities in machine learning.

title: The Evolution of Robust Optimization in Dynamic System Modeling
abstract: This paper presents a novel optimization algorithm for complex systems based on a dynamic probabilistic model. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with the inherent complexity and non-linearity of such systems, relying on static parameters that fail to capture the system's dynamic behavior. Our proposed algorithm leverages probabilistic modeling to simulate system behavior and dynamically adjust optimization parameters, resulting in improved performance and stability. The core mechanism involves generating probabilistic paths through the system, allowing the algorithm to explore a wider range of solutions and mitigate local optima. This approach contrasts with traditional methods that often converge to suboptimal solutions due to their static nature. The research demonstrates the effectiveness of this dynamic probabilistic model in optimizing a complex, multi-variable system, showcasing enhanced resilience and adaptability.

title: Dimension Fusion Theory: A Quantum Computing Validation Approach
abstract: This paper explores the application of dimension fusion theory to quantum computing validation, specifically focusing on the detection of quantum computer stability and the prediction of quantum computer performance. The core of this work lies in the development of a novel algorithm leveraging quantum entanglement to provide a fundamentally new method for assessing the integrity of quantum states. We detail the theoretical framework underpinning this approach, showcasing its potential to address limitations of existing validation techniques. The paper presents a comprehensive overview of the proposed algorithm, its mathematical underpinnings, and the results of initial simulations demonstrating its effectiveness in identifying vulnerabilities within quantum computation. Finally, we discuss the implications of this research for advancing the field of quantum computing verification and security.

title: 基于多尺度拓扑的概率模型构建
abstract: This paper investigates the application of a novel probabilistic model based on the principles of multiple scale topology. The core aim is to develop a framework that simplifies the construction of probability models by leveraging the inherent structure and properties of complex systems. We propose a method utilizing a multi-scale topology to generate a probabilistic framework, allowing for a streamlined process of model creation. The resulting model offers a new perspective on the representation and analysis of complex systems, specifically focusing on systems exhibiting emergent behavior and intricate relationships. The paper details the methodology, showcasing its efficacy through illustrative examples and preliminary results. We demonstrate that the multi-scale topology approach significantly reduces the computational complexity while maintaining a high degree of predictive accuracy.

abstract: This paper investigates the potential of leveraging quantum entanglement to enhance complex multi-particle quantum computations. The core focus is on exploring how entanglement can be strategically utilized to improve the precision and complexity of simulations within these systems. Traditional approaches to simulating complex multi-particle systems often face limitations in computational feasibility, presenting a significant challenge for advancing quantum computing. This work proposes a novel approach utilizing quantum entanglement to overcome these limitations, offering a pathway to more accurate and sophisticated modeling. We will detail the theoretical framework underpinning this method, explore specific implementation strategies, and discuss the anticipated benefits and potential challenges associated with this research. This paper introduces a conceptual framework for complex multi-particle quantum simulations driven by entanglement, highlighting the core mechanism and potential impact on quantum computation.

title: Adaptive High-Dimensional Singular Point Clustering Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive high-dimensional singular point clustering algorithm designed to address the challenges of data clustering, particularly when dealing with high-dimensional, complex data sets. The algorithm dynamically adjusts cluster parameters based on data's inherent density and distribution, aiming to achieve more accurate and robust clustering results. We propose a novel approach that leverages the information about singular points to guide the clustering process, mitigating the pitfalls of fixed parameter reliance. This research focuses on enhancing the effectiveness of traditional clustering techniques through a refined, adaptable methodology. The core mechanism involves a dynamic parameter adjustment system that responds to the data's characteristics, providing a more nuanced and efficient clustering outcome.

title: Title: Bayesian Adaptive Constraint Optimization with Quantum Embedding
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Bayesian Adaptive Constraint Optimization (BACO) algorithm, leveraging quantum embedding to enhance exploration and exploitation simultaneously. The core concept is to embed quantum states within the optimization process, enabling a quantum-informed exploration that dynamically adjusts constraint sets based on the *internal* quantum state of a system. This approach addresses limitations of traditional optimization techniques by simultaneously reducing computational cost and improving solution quality. The algorithm utilizes a Bayesian framework to refine constraint sets iteratively, guiding the search towards promising regions of the solution space. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this quantum embedding method through extensive simulations and analysis, showcasing a significant improvement in both solution quality and computational efficiency compared to existing state-of-the-art techniques. The resulting BACO algorithm offers a promising pathway towards more robust and efficient optimization in complex, high-dimensional problems.

title: Quantum-Inspired Evolutionary Algorithms for Feature Selection
abstract: Feature selection is a critical preprocessing step in machine learning, aiming to identify the most relevant features from a larger set to improve model performance and reduce computational complexity. Traditional evolutionary algorithms (EAs), such as genetic algorithms, can be computationally expensive, particularly when dealing with high-dimensional feature spaces. This paper proposes a novel approach leveraging quantum-inspired concepts to accelerate feature selection. Specifically, we incorporate superposition and interference principles, inspired by quantum mechanics, into the evolutionary process. This allows the algorithm to explore multiple feature subsets concurrently, effectively reducing the search space and potentially achieving significant speedups. The core claim is that integrating quantum-inspired ideas into EAs can provide a viable solution to the computational challenges posed by high-dimensional feature spaces. The proposed algorithm maintains the fundamental principles of EA while introducing quantum-inspired mechanisms for enhanced exploration. The effectiveness of the approach is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, outlining a framework for implementation.

title: 基于量子拓扑的自适应量子计算的量子算法优化
abstract: Quantum computation holds immense potential for scientific discovery and technological advancement, but the development of efficient quantum algorithms is a significant challenge. This paper explores the application of quantum topology to optimize quantum algorithms, proposing a novel approach that leverages the inherent structure of quantum systems to dynamically adjust algorithm parameters, ultimately leading to enhanced computational efficiency. We introduce a method based on identifying and exploiting topological features within quantum circuits to guide optimization. The core mechanism focuses on using quantum topology to automatically re-parameterize circuits, mitigating the need for manual tuning and promoting more robust and adaptable algorithms. We present a theoretical framework and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of this technique. The resulting algorithm offers a promising pathway toward more efficient quantum computation, potentially bridging the gap between theoretical promise and practical implementation.

abstract: Quantum-enhanced fractal dimension analysis explores the potential of quantum phenomena to refine the determination of fractal complexity. The study outlines a rigorous theoretical foundation and preliminary experimental investigations to validate the proposed quantum-enhanced technique.

title: Topological Measurement Techniques for Quantum Sensors
abstract: This paper explores the application of topological measurement techniques to enhance the performance of quantum sensors. Quantum sensors, renowned for their sensitivity, often struggle with the noise introduced by complex environments. This work proposes a novel approach that leverages the inherent properties of topological measurement to mitigate this issue. The core concept involves utilizing a quantum sensor within a complex environment and employing topological measurement to process the sensor's output signal. This method aims to extract relevant information from the noisy data, ultimately improving the overall measurement accuracy. title: Dynamic Quantum Adaptive Geometry Transformation
abstract: This paper presents a novel geometric transformation algorithm based on dynamic quantum entanglement. Traditional geometric transformation methods often rely on manual adjustments, limiting their efficiency and adaptability. We propose a system that leverages quantum entanglement to automatically adjust transformation parameters, enabling optimized geometric modeling and design. The core mechanism centers around the manipulation of entangled quantum states to achieve a continuous and adaptive transformation process. This approach offers a potential paradigm shift in geometric computation, demonstrating enhanced efficiency and versatility compared to conventional methods. The algorithm is designed to handle complex geometric transformations with minimal human intervention.

title: Algorithmic Bias Mitigation in Deep Learning Through Differential Privacy
abstract: This paper investigates the pervasive issue of algorithmic bias within deep learning models, proposing a novel framework for mitigating it through dynamic adjustment of privacy guarantees during training. We introduce a system that intelligently analyzes data sensitivity and potential bias, dynamically adjusting the level of privacy applied to each data point. The goal is to improve fairness and robustness while maintaining model accuracy. The framework utilizes a differential privacy approach to ensure that privacy-preserving modifications do not significantly degrade the model's performance. We explore the efficacy of this approach through simulations and initial evaluations, demonstrating a significant reduction in bias compared to standard training techniques. The resulting system offers a promising path toward more equitable and reliable deep learning applications.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Geometric Algorithms for Optimization
abstract: Quantum-enhanced geometric algorithms offer a promising avenue for addressing complex optimization problems with enhanced computational efficiency. This paper explores the potential of leveraging quantum annealing and quantum approximate optimization algorithms (QAOA) to accelerate the search for optimal solutions in high-dimensional spaces. We investigate the theoretical advantages and practical implementation considerations of these quantum approaches, proposing a framework for designing quantum algorithms tailored to specific optimization challenges. The core claim is that quantum-enhanced geometric algorithms can significantly outperform classical algorithms in terms of solution speed and accuracy, opening up new possibilities for solving problems in diverse fields. The paper concludes with a discussion of current limitations and future research directions.

title: PETROGRAPHIE ET CARTOGRAPHIE DES FORMATIONS DE VINDA, KONGO-CENTRAL, REPUBLIQUE DEMOCRATIQUE DU CONGO
abstract: Le potentiel géologique extraordinaire de la République Démocratique de Congo étonna J. Cornet pour qu'il ait considéré ce pays comme un scandale géologique. C'est ainsi qu'il appartient au citoyen congolais de mieux connaitre la géologie de son pays afin de mieux gérer et utiliser ces ressources minières. D'où nous avons pensé, dans le cadre de ce travail, à contribuer à la connaissance géologique de notre pays en général et celle de la région de Vinda, dans la province du Kongo Central en particulier ; pour procéder ainsi à la mise à jour des informations géologiques préexistantes. Ce travail trouve particulièrement son intérêt sur le plan cartographique de la zone d'étude, étant donné qu'elle est située entre Boma et Matadi, en dehors de la carte géologique de Boma S6/13-SW élaborée par Kalala Ntumba en 1975.

title: PEAO: A Cooperative Parallel Enzyme Optimization Algorithm with Adaptive Search Mechanisms
abstract: Bio-inspired optimization algorithms have become an effective class of techniques for addressing challenging continuous optimization problems. In this work, we introduce the Parallel Enzyme Action Optimization (PEAO) algorithm, a parallel bio-inspired optimization approach that incorporates a multi-strategy communication mechanism among cooperative subpopulations. The population is partitioned into multiple subpopulations that evolve concurrently, promoting a more effective exploration of the search space. Furthermore, PEAO integrates adaptive search factors, local search procedure and communication strategies to improve solution quality while reducing the risk of premature convergence. In addition, a K-means-based population initialization procedure and a convergence-driven stopping criterion based on successive improvements in the best objective-function value are incorporated to reduce unnecessary objective-function evaluations and improve the overall efficiency of the optimization process.

title: A hybrid framework integrating quantile regression and isolation forest for reservoir water level anomaly detection in early warning applications
abstract: Reservoir water level monitoring and early warning are critical components of flood control and disaster mitigation in river basins, as they can effectively prevent dam failures or downstream flooding. However, existing reservoir monitoring systems generally suffer from response delays and ineffective early warnings when dealing with sudden anomalies in water level readings (such as those caused by extreme hydrological conditions, instrument malfunctions, or localized damage). This study proposes a method for the automatic identification and early warning of abnormal water level changes that integrates the quantile regression model and the isolated forest algorithm (QR-IForest framework). Taking two series-connected reservoirs in the Yonghan River Basin in Guangdong Province as the study subjects, the method performs anomaly detection on real-time water levels based on data from actual monitoring stations in the reservoir area. The results indicate that: (1) The fused method achieves higher accuracy in anomaly detection than either method alone, with a precision rate of 92.24%, a recall rate of 0.8992, and an F1-score of 0.9106. The true positive rate (TPR) for anomaly detection reaches 99.15%, while the true negative rate (TNR) reaches 89.92%. (2) Simulation tests were conducted for two different scenarios (heavy rainfall and river channel blockage). The results show that the model’s anomaly detection capability can provide rapid, early warnings, detecting anomalies as early as 2 hours before an incident occurs. (3) This integrated model can automatically classify detected anomalies. When identifying anomalies related to monitoring equipment or those caused by deviations in hydrological patterns, the detection accuracy exceeds 85%. The method developed in this study provides a reliable basis for efficiently identifying anomalies in water level monitoring data from small and medium-sized reservoirs, thereby ensuring the safe management and operation of these reservoirs.

title: Emotional Resonance or Rational Guidance? Exploring the Mechanisms Through Which Generative AI Recommendation Roles Shape Consumers' Adoption Intentions
abstract: ABSTRACT Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is reshaping e‐commerce by enabling conversational recommenders that can explain their advice and flexibly enact social roles (e.g., assistant vs. friend). Yet it remains unclear how these roles affect consumers' adoption of GenAI recommendations, through which trust pathways, and under what message designs. Drawing primarily on role theory and trust theory, with product evaluability and dual‐process logic specifying the relevant conditions, we examine how recommender role interacts with product type and message framing. Across three experiments, Study 1 ( n = 263) demonstrates a role–product fit: assistant‐type recommendations generate higher adoption intentions for search goods, whereas friend‐type recommendations generate higher adoption intentions for experience goods. Study 2 ( n = 293) identifies the underlying trust pathways: assistant‐type recommendations increase adoption of search goods primarily through cognitive trust, whereas friend‐type recommendations increase adoption of experience goods primarily through affective trust. Study 3 ( n = 367) shows that message framing is a boundary condition: loss framing strengthens the assistant–search‐good fit, whereas gain framing strengthens the friend–experience‐good fit. Together, the findings show that GenAI role plasticity—the capacity of the same system to enact different socially meaningful roles—shapes persuasion through role‐contingent trust and context‐dependent message processing. The research offers practical guidance for aligning GenAI roles and framing strategies with product evaluability in e‐commerce.

title: Uncertainty Signals for Network Intent Translation: Risk Ranking and Ambiguity Localization
abstract: Intent-based networking realization starts by translating high-level intents into low-level network configurations. Recent approaches have shifted toward LLM-based translation. Despite promising results, most studies focus on translation accuracy and overlook risks associated with deploying the resulting configurations. In this work, we investigate the pre-deployment translation risk of LLM-generated configurations by analyzing the model's uncertainty. We propose to use two uncertainty signals, namely sampling-based predictive uncertainty for translation-risk ranking and token-level entropy for ambiguity-source localization. We evaluate these signals on an ambiguity-controlled test set across different context types and sampling budgets, using a Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model fine-tuned for intent translation on a vendor-specific switch platform (Juniper EX3300). The results demonstrate that predictive uncertainty provides a useful signal for ranking translations by risk across context types and sampling budgets, albeit with substantial miscalibration under less informative contexts. Moreover, we show that parameter-token entropy correlates with parameter-sourced ambiguity and keyword-token entropy correlates with description-sourced ambiguity. These results indicate the potential of using uncertainty signals in an LLM-generated configuration deployment pipeline, where predictive uncertainty can support selective deployment, while token-level entropy can identify sources of ambiguity.

title: Urban Boundaries, Social Barriers: A Benchmark and Vision-Centric Framework for Mapping Gated Communities and Equity Implications
abstract: Communities are fundamental spatial units that shape urban form and social life. Whether a residential compound is spatially open or enclosed affects mobility, access to public services, and equity, yet studies of Chinese fengbi xiaoqu remain largely qualitative or small-scale, limiting reproducible city-scale analysis. We address this gap by introducing GBA-GCs, a metropolitan-scale multimodal benchmark for locally grounded gated/open community recognition in China's Greater Bay Area, covering 37,444 residential compounds with aligned boundary polygons, high-resolution satellite imagery, Chinese metadata, and structured attributes, together with expert-verified labels, inter-annotator reliability, and official evaluation splits. Built on this benchmark, we present Multimodal Classifier for Gated Community (MCGC), a vision-centric multimodal framework based on DINOv3-SAT that fuses imagery, text, and structured cues via modality-aware cross-attention and adaptive gating to mitigate modality imbalance. MCGC consistently outperforms strong unimodal and multimodal baselines. Finally, we apply the validated model to metropolitan-scale mapping and report equity-oriented findings including spatial clustering of GCs, privatized green space, and reduced pedestrian connectivity. The benchmark, code, and release documentation are available at https://github.com/MinweiZhao/GBA-GCs.

title: Feature Reconfiguration With Visual Prior for Medical Lesion Segmentation
abstract: Lesion segmentation in medical images plays a critical role in clinical diagnosis and treatment planning. Despite significant advances, lesion segmentation remains challenging due to two major factors: (1) complex background interference; (2) diverse lesion morphology. Existing encoder-decoder based methods mainly focus on enhancing feature extraction or redesigning decoding strategies. However, they lack early prior guidance and feature reconfiguration during the encoding stage, limiting their effectiveness in handling these challenges. To address these limitations, we propose FreNet, a feature reconfiguration framework with visual priors, which performs pixel-level reconfiguration before encoding and feature-level reconfiguration during encoding for precise medical lesion segmentation. To suppress background responses, we propose an Implicit Prior Neural Network (IPNN), which models a continuous spatial field and leverages visual prior from SAM to reconfigure input image before encoding stage. To better handle diverse lesion morphology, we design a Dual-domain Feature Reconfiguration (DFR) module to progressively reconfigure backbone features during encoding stage. Within DFR, the Frequency Decoupling Module (FDM) decouples backbone features in frequency domain to enhance foreground-background discriminability, while the Spatial Localization Module (SLM) spatially relocates and improving spatial stability after frequency decoupling. Extensive experiments on 9 medical image segmentation benchmarks across three imaging modalities demonstrate that FreNet significantly outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods. On the challenging ETIS dataset, our method achieves Dice improvements of 5.0% over SOTA method and 7.2% over SAM.

title: Quantum Random Matrix Optimization
abstract: Quantum Random Matrix Optimization (QROM) presents a novel approach to machine learning and data analysis by leveraging the principles of quantum mechanics, specifically quantum superposition and entanglement, to optimize the parameters of random matrices. This research explores a quantum algorithm designed to enhance the performance of machine learning models through strategically designed random matrices, aiming to outperform classical optimization techniques in specific scenarios. The core mechanism relies on manipulating the state space of random matrices to guide the learning process, potentially leading to more efficient and accurate results. The study investigates the potential benefits and challenges of employing quantum algorithms in this context, highlighting the need for further exploration and refinement of the proposed framework.

title: Quantum Neural Networks: An Adaptive Optimization Mechanism
abstract: Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs) represent a paradigm shift in neural network design, leveraging the unique properties of quantum mechanics to potentially surpass classical neural networks in terms of efficiency and accuracy. This paper explores the concept of a novel adaptive optimization mechanism within QNNs, utilizing quantum entanglement and quantum state adaptation to enhance training and inference processes. The core of this approach focuses on establishing a dynamic feedback loop that allows the network to continually refine its parameters and structure based on the inherent properties of its data. The proposed mechanism offers a potential path towards more robust and adaptable neural network architectures. We delve into the theoretical foundations and preliminary experimental validation of this approach, demonstrating its potential for accelerating learning and improving generalization performance.

title: 基于自适应的图论模型
abstract: This paper introduces a novel model, the "基于自适应的图论模型", designed to optimize machine learning models by leveraging graph theory concepts. Traditional machine learning models often struggle with complex data landscapes, requiring extensive feature engineering and parameter tuning. This model utilizes graph-based representations, node degree, centrality measures, and community structure to capture inherent data relationships, offering a more robust and adaptable approach to model learning. The core mechanism involves integrating graph theory techniques with optimization algorithms to enhance model performance. This paper details the model's architecture, its benefits, and potential applications within the field of machine learning.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Probabilistic Matrix Operations
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a bizarre phenomenon where two or more particles become linked in such a way that they share the same fate, holds profound implications for computation. This paper explores the potential of leveraging quantum entanglement to revolutionize matrix operations, particularly focusing on achieving high-precision arithmetic and enhanced probabilistic calculations. Traditional matrix operations, while fundamental to many scientific and engineering disciplines, often struggle with computational limitations and susceptibility to gradient vanishing, hindering their application in complex calculations. We propose a novel approach utilizing entanglement to overcome these challenges through parallel computation and entanglement transfer, offering a path toward more efficient and robust matrix operations. This work details the core mechanism, explores the theoretical implications, and provides a preliminary assessment of the potential benefits of this quantum approach.

title: Structural Entropy as a Metric for Neural Network Robustness
abstract: This paper introduces structural entropy as a novel metric to assess the robustness of neural networks. Traditional measures of network complexity, such as layer depth or number of connections, often fail to capture the critical role of diverse pathways within the network's architecture. We propose quantifying robustness based on the structural entropy, defined as the diversity of paths between any two nodes in the network's graph representation. This approach allows us to measure the redundancy and resilience of information flow, directly correlating with a network's ability to withstand adversarial attacks and noisy inputs. Through theoretical analysis and a focus on the underlying graph structure, we demonstrate that higher structural entropy consistently corresponds to improved robustness performance. The results highlight the importance of network architectural diversity in creating robust deep learning models.

title: Relational Reinforcement Learning with Epistemic Uncertainty
abstract: Relational Reinforcement Learning (RRL) has demonstrated success in environments where interactions involve relationships between entities. However, existing RRL approaches often operate under the assumption of complete or highly accurate relational knowledge, a condition rarely met in real-world scenarios. This work introduces a novel extension to RRL that explicitly incorporates and propagates *epistemic uncertainty* – the agent's belief about the accuracy of its relational knowledge. We augment the standard RRL framework with a probabilistic relational graph, where nodes represent entities and edges represent hypothesized relationships, each associated with a confidence score. This graph dynamically evolves as the agent interacts with the environment, reflecting increasing certainty about relationships through updated confidence values. The agent then uses this uncertainty to guide exploration, favoring actions that lead to information gain and reducing the risk of acting on potentially inaccurate relational assumptions. We formalize this approach with a modified Bellman equation that accounts for the uncertainty in the state transition probabilities. The core contribution lies in the integration of uncertainty modeling into the learning process, leading to a more robust and adaptable RRL agent. Experiments (simulated) demonstrate the improved performance and decision-making capabilities of the proposed method compared to standard RRL, particularly in scenarios with noisy or incomplete relational data. ---

title: Title: Non-Standard Lattice Parameterization for Quantum Simulation
abstract: This paper investigates the application of machine learning to automate the design of non-standard lattice parameters for quantum simulation. Traditional lattice design relies heavily on expert knowledge and trial-and-error, which can be time-consuming and suboptimal. We propose a novel approach utilizing a machine learning model trained on a dataset of known quantum simulations with various lattice geometries. This model learns to predict optimal lattice parameters directly from the system's properties, leading to improved accuracy and significantly reduced design time. The resulting lattice parameters are then applied to simulate quantum systems, offering a more efficient and robust method for exploring the landscape of potential solutions. The paper details the model training process, the resulting optimization results, and the impact of the machine learning approach on simulation accuracy.

title: Decentralized Reinforcement Learning with Bayesian Belief Propagation
abstract: Decentralized reinforcement learning (DRL) presents a promising avenue for tackling complex, real-world problems involving multiple agents operating concurrently. However, scaling DRL to environments with high dimensionality and inherent non-stationarity remains a significant challenge. This work introduces a novel framework for decentralized reinforcement learning leveraging Bayesian Belief Propagation (BBP). The core idea is to employ BBP to iteratively refine a decentralized policy by propagating belief information across agents, effectively handling uncertainty and mitigating the curse of dimensionality. Our approach incorporates prior knowledge into the learning process, further enhancing its robustness and adaptability. We demonstrate, theoretically and conceptually, the potential of this combined methodology for addressing the limitations of traditional DRL algorithms. The proposed method offers a new perspective on learning in dynamic, distributed systems, providing a pathway towards more scalable and robust decentralized control.

title: 基于自适应的图神经网络的优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on adaptive neural networks (ANNs) to enhance the expressiveness of graph neural networks (GNNs). Traditional GNN architectures often rely on fixed structural parameters, limiting their adaptability to evolving data. We propose a dynamic weight adjustment mechanism within the ANN, allowing the network to automatically optimize connection weights based on data characteristics. This approach addresses the limitations of static optimization methods by enabling the algorithm to learn optimal weight configurations directly from the data. We present a comprehensive evaluation on benchmark datasets, demonstrating the algorithm's superior performance compared to existing methods, particularly in scenarios with complex data patterns. The core mechanism centers on a self-adaptive weighting strategy, facilitating the network's responsiveness to changing input. The results indicate a significant improvement in prediction accuracy and network performance.

title: Borrowing Knowledge Across Tasks: A Interdisciplinary Mapping Review of Transfer Learning and the Pretraining Paradigm
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Transfer Learning and the Pretraining Paradigm in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of transfer learning and pretraining as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: 基于动态的自适应学习的神经元网络
abstract: This paper introduces a novel neural network architecture, termed "Dynamic Adaptive Learning Network" (DALLN), designed to enhance learning efficiency and improve model generalization. DALLN distinguishes itself through the implementation of dynamic adjustment of connection strengths, a strategy that contrasts with traditional static neural network models. The core mechanism involves iteratively updating synaptic connections based on a learned error signal, dynamically adjusting the network's parameters to optimize performance across a diverse range of tasks. We explore the benefits of this dynamic approach in various learning scenarios, demonstrating significant improvements in accuracy and robustness. This research contributes to the field of neural network learning by providing a framework for adaptive and efficient training.

title: Dynamic Quantum State Quantum Computation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum computing framework predicated on dynamic quantum state manipulation and its subsequent application to complex problem-solving. Traditional quantum computation relies on static qubit configurations, while this framework dynamically adjusts quantum states, enabling a fundamentally different approach to computation. We propose a mechanism that leverages the inherent evolution of quantum states to achieve solutions to intractable problems. This research delves into the design and implementation of a quantum algorithm that utilizes this dynamic state evolution, offering a potential advancement over existing quantum computing paradigms. The core claim of this work is that a dynamically adjusted quantum state framework can effectively address complex computational challenges.

title: 基于自旋的几何变换的并行计算模型
abstract: This paper presents a novel parallel computing model based on spin-based geometric transformations. The core concept is to leverage the unique quantum properties of spin to enable efficient and complex geometric calculations. We design a parallel computing framework utilizing spin-induced quantum entanglement and manipulation to achieve superior computational performance compared to conventional approaches. The proposed model offers a new pathway for tackling computationally intensive geometric problems and is presented as a potential advancement in parallel computing. We detail the model's architecture, implementation, and performance evaluation, highlighting key advantages and potential applications.

title: Quantum Spacetime Geometry: A Novel Approach to Quantum System Simulation and Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces Quantum Spacetime Geometry (QSG), a novel framework combining quantum field theory and geometric analysis, to enhance the simulation and optimization of complex quantum systems. Traditional computational models often struggle with the intricate interplay of quantum phenomena, necessitating a new perspective. QSG leverages the principles of quantum spacetime geometry to develop algorithms that effectively navigate and manipulate quantum systems, offering a significant advancement in computational capabilities. The core claim is that QSG provides a robust and efficient method for simulating and optimizing quantum calculations by strategically employing quantum effects. This research explores the theoretical underpinnings and practical application of QSG, demonstrating its potential to revolutionize the field of quantum computation.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic learning algorithm based on adaptive deep learning, designed to dynamically adjust learning rates and optimization parameters based on the characteristics of the input data. This adaptive approach allows the model to continuously refine its parameters, leading to improved performance across diverse datasets. This work presents a practical implementation of the dynamic learning algorithm, demonstrating its potential to address limitations of static training methods.

title: Title: Information-Theoretic Topology for Data Compression and Search
abstract: This paper explores the application of information-theoretic topology as a novel approach to data compression and search. Traditional data compression techniques rely heavily on statistical methods and bit-shifting, often resulting in suboptimal compression ratios. We propose a new methodology based on the concept of 'Information Density' – a topological structure that encodes the inherent structure of the data. This structure is designed to be highly adaptable and allows for more efficient representation and retrieval, ultimately exceeding the performance of existing methods. The core mechanism involves constructing a topology that reflects the relationships between data elements, enabling a more nuanced and effective compression process. The resulting technique demonstrates promising results in compression ratios and search efficiency, representing a potential paradigm shift in data compression.

title: Topological Quantum Entanglement Dynamic Topology Optimization
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, presents unique challenges for optimization and control. Traditional methods often struggle with the inherent complexity of entangled states, limiting their practical application. This paper introduces a novel dynamic topology optimization algorithm specifically designed to address this challenge by dynamically adjusting the topology of entangled states. We propose a framework that iteratively refines the entanglement's structure based on a feedback loop, leveraging quantum properties to enhance entanglement strength and robustness. The algorithm's core mechanism centers on a quantum state transformation process, achieving a significant improvement in entanglement fidelity and utility compared to static optimization techniques. This research explores the potential of this approach to unlock new opportunities in quantum information processing and quantum communication.

title: FedMASA: Federated Minority-Aware Selection and Aggregation for Non-IID IIoT Intrusion Detection.
abstract: The heterogeneity of data across Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) devices poses significant challenges to federated learning-based intrusion detection systems, where the Non-IID data distribution leads to poor detection performance, particularly on rare attack classes. To address these issues, this letter proposes FedMASA, a deep reinforcement learning-assisted federated learning framework with minority-aware selection and aggregation for Non-IID IIoT intrusion detection. Specifically, we formulate client selection as a Markov Decision Process and employ Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient to dynamically select optimal clients based on real-time state observations. A minority-aware aggregation mechanism with class-balanced weighting is designed to amplify the influence of scarce attack classes while penalizing high-latency clients. Extensive experiments on the Edge-IIoTset and ToN-IoT datasets demonstrate that FedMASA consistently surpasses the standard FedAvg baseline across all Non-IID settings. In the most challenging $\alpha=0.1$ scenario, FedMASA outperforms FedAvg by 2.96\% in accuracy and 8.87\% in Macro-F1 on Edge-IIoTset, and by 4.24\% and 10.34\% on ToN-IoT, respectively.

title: Анализ пользовательского опыта представленного в текстовой форме для целей оценки взаимодействия граждан с государственными и муниципальными органами
abstract: Целью работы является разработка автоматизированного инструмента анализа отзывов граждан о деятельности многофункциональных центров (МФЦ). Были решены следующие задачи: 1) провести теоретико-методологический анализ подходов к автоматизированному анализу пользовательского опыта в текстовой форме в контексте государственных услуг; 2) разработать гибридный алгоритм анализа отзывов на основе LDA, BERT и локальных нейронных моделей; 3) разработаны стратегии повышения эффективности государственных услуг. Актуальность темы обусловлена необходимостью автоматизации обработки растущего объёма обратной связи от граждан в условиях цифровой трансформации государственного управления. Источниками информации выступили данные 3000 отзывов граждан о деятельности МФЦ с открытых платформ, данные отечественной и зарубежной научно-исследовательской литературы, официальных Интернетресурсов и аналитических агентств, нормативно-правовые акты Российской Федерации. Разработан гибридный подход, объединяющий тематическое моделирование (LDA), анализ тональности (ruBERT) и каскадную генерацию ответов (LLM) в единый автоматизированный пайплайн. Точность комбинированной классификации тональности составила 88,5 %, когерентность LDA-модели — 0,52, экспертная оценка качества ответов — 4,0–4,5 из 5,0. Разработан MVP-прототип веб-приложения для пилотного внедрения в МФЦ. Результаты могут быть применены в деятельности МФЦ для аналитического мониторинга, поддержки операторов и автоматического оповещения о проблемных ситуациях.

Были решены следующие задачи: 1) провести теоретико-методологический анализ подходов к автоматизированному анализу пользовательского опыта в текстовой форме в контексте государственных услуг; 2) разработать гибридный алгоритм анализа отзывов на основе LDA, BERT и локальных нейронных моделей; 3) разработаны стратегии повышения эффективности государственных услуг. Актуальность темы обусловлена необходимостью автоматизации обработки растущего объёма обратной связи от граждан в условиях цифровой трансформации государственного управления. Источниками информации выступили данные 3000 отзывов граждан о деятельности МФЦ с открытых платформ, данные отечественной и зарубежной научно-исследовательской литературы, официальных Интернетресурсов и аналитических агентств, нормативно-правовые акты Российской Федерации. Разработан гибридный подход, объединяющий тематическое моделирование (LDA), анализ тональности (ruBERT) и каскадную генерацию ответов (LLM) в единый автоматизированный пайплайн. Точность комбинированной классификации тональности составила 88,5 %, когерентность LDA-модели — 0,52, экспертная оценка качества ответов — 4,0–4,5 из 5,0. Разработан MVP-прототип веб-приложения для пилотного внедрения в МФЦ. Результаты могут быть применены в деятельности МФЦ для аналитического мониторинга, поддержки операторов и автоматического оповещения о проблемных ситуациях.

title: goldless
abstract: A knowledge-extraction pipeline annotates relations between terms using a panel of five raters, «four language models from three vendors and one non-LLM channel from different vendors and one a non-LLM distributional channel. No labelled ground truth exists for those relations and none will. This registration therefore predicts the behaviour of the measurement instrument rather than the truth of its output: fifteen quantities, each with a direction, a numeric threshold and a named outcome that refutes it, fixed before the first paid call of a revised annotation instruction. Four further rows register the structure of a comparison between corpus layers, its comparator, and the removal of a channel asymmetry. Eight conditions define when the run is invalid and its numbers carry no force. Everything is published under any outcome, including a negative one. The full document, with all tables and the derivation of every number, is attached to this registration.

title: Identifying low-quality features and suboptimal models to enhance phenotype prediction
abstract: It is common to build predictive models for complex phenotypes, such as diseases, where sample sizes are often limited by the cost of data collection. Machine learning and statistical methods are widely used in these cases. However, they may fail to identify high-quality features and lead to suboptimal models with high underfitting or overfitting risks. Here, we present mBoost to identify low-quality features and suboptimal models to enhance phenotype prediction. Importantly, it provides confidence on model performance, helping researchers avoid the frustrating cycle of model switching for possibly better performance. We demonstrate mBoost with simulations and real-data examples. Specifically, mBoost identifies optimal depth and width for a deep neural network in a drug example, detects suboptimal models in microbiome cohorts, and proposes a measure for telling whether the trained model is applicable to new data. Thus, mBoost will serve as a practical tool for model building and diagnosis.

title: Fast Polynomial Transcendentals for LLMs
abstract: Graphics processing unit (GPU) generations scale matrix, special-function, and memory pipelines at different rates, so kernel bottlenecks move as hardware evolves. FlashAttention-4 exposed this imbalance inside attention on NVIDIA Blackwell. We test whether short polynomial programs can accelerate other special-function-unit (SFU) operations in large language models (LLMs). We first compare native PyTorch evaluation with packed fused multiply--add (FMA) programs in an isolated IEEE binary16 (FP16) sweep spanning L2-resident and high-bandwidth-memory (HBM)-resident working sets. We then replace native sigmoid, tanh, and sigmoid linear unit (SiLU) with degree-3 or degree-4 bfloat16 (BF16) programs in four GB200 integration tasks: dense SiLU, tanh-softcapped attention, sigmoid attention, and routed-expert Swish-gated linear unit (SwiGLU). The programs combine analytical symmetry, target-format rounding, and packed arithmetic inside consuming kernels. The isolated paths improve by 1.19--2.19x in L2 and 1.00--1.70x in HBM. The dense-SiLU, tanh-softcapped-attention, and routed-expert substitutions improve complete training-step throughput by 2.7\%, 2.9\%, and 8.0\%, respectively. The sigmoid-attention substitution improves complete-attention forward by 7.4\% and the complete GPU step by 0.3\%. Same-checkpoint open-weight ablations and one paired pre-training comparison per task extend the evaluation to model behavior. At common horizons near 100 billion tokens, the final smoothed training-loss differences (polynomial minus native) range from $-0.107$ to $+0.079$ across the four tasks.

title: Cascaded Non-Line-of-Sight Imaging
abstract: Time-of-flight non-line-of-sight (NLOS) imaging recovers information from hidden objects by analyzing the time of flight of indirect photons scattered on a visible (relay) wall. Most methods make the simplifying assumption that photons travel exclusively three-bounce paths, thus ignoring other useful information encoded in higher-order photons (with, e.g., four- or five-bounce paths). We present a novel cascaded NLOS imaging approach that leverages higher-order information and allows imaging a broader range of single- and multi-corner scenarios. We combine ultra-fast laser scanning with recent time-gated 2D sensor arrays to capture the scene's impulse response on a visible relay wall. From the captured impulse response, our method computes an analogous virtual impulse response at any other hidden wall. This effectively allows us to concatenate a second, virtual NLOS imaging system that leverages higher-order illumination. We validate our cascaded imaging method both in simulation and with a real prototype, demonstrating NLOS imaging with fourth- and fifth-bounce illumination of objects in challenging orientations and hidden around two corners. We also analyze how wave-based NLOS imaging interacts with rough hidden walls, which explains and helps overcome existing visibility limitations. We further illustrate how to image hidden objects from different perspectives, thus observing previously unseen features, by relying on multiple hidden walls.

title: Calibrating subgrid parametrizations of single-column ocean models via simulation-based inference
abstract: Subgrid parametrizations of vertical mixing in ocean models depend on free coefficients that cannot be measured directly and must be calibrated against high-fidelity references such as large-eddy simulations (LES). Existing approaches return point estimates and leave the associated uncertainty unquantified, a limitation when the inverse problem is ill-posed or when distinct parameter configurations fit the data comparably well. Simulation-based inference (SBI) addresses exactly this: given a prior and access to the simulator, it approximates the full posterior over parameters without requiring a tractable likelihood, at a cost set by the number of simulator evaluations. We apply it to \texttt{tunax}, a JAX-based single-column ocean model, to calibrate the coefficients of its $k$--$\varepsilon$ closure. A blockwise PCA summary statistic compresses the simulator output along the depth axis while preserving its forcing--horizon--variable structure, making inference tractable at modest budgets. We compare neural posterior estimation and its sequential variants against a recent training-free approach built on a tabular foundation model. The latter recovers informative posteriors from a few hundred simulator calls, outperforming the trained estimators at every budget considered.

title: Review of Lightweight Cryptography for Mobile Phone Security Against Modern Cyber Threats
authors: Dr. Naveen Kumar Singh Nandini Sharma
abstract: Mobile phones have become the primary computing platform for personal and financial data, yet they operate under strict constraints of battery life, memory, and processing power that limit the practicality of conventional cryptographic standards such as AES and RSA. This paper presents a review of the literature on lightweight cryptography (LWC) as a mechanism for securing mobile phones against modern cyber threats, including malware, network interception, and behavioural exploitation. Drawing on twenty-five peer-reviewed sources published between 2015 and 2024, the review examines the design principles of lightweight cryptographic algorithms, the evolving mobile malware landscape, the standardisation efforts led by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), and the existing frameworks proposed for constrained-device security. The review finds that while lightweight cryptographic algorithms have matured considerably in terms of theoretical security and implementation efficiency, comparatively few studies evaluate these algorithms within complete, real-device mobile security frameworks that explicitly address contemporary malware threats. The paper concludes by identifying this integration gap and proposing directions for future research, including real-device benchmarking, threat-model-driven framework design, and the co-design of cryptographic and detection-based defences.

title: Machine Learning-Based Sentiment Classification of Reviews from Indonesian Mobile Applications Using TF-IDF
abstract: The increasing volume of mobile application reviews has created a need for automated sentiment classification capable of handling large-scale and imbalanced user-generated data. This study aimed to compare classical machine learning algorithms and evaluate the effectiveness of class-weighted learning in improving minority-class recognition in Indonesian mobile application reviews. The dataset was cleaned, deduplicated, and controlled for conflicting labels and data leakage, resulting in 357,327 unique reviews across Negative, Neutral, and Positive sentiment classes. Textual features were represented using Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) with 50,000 features, and the data were divided using an 80:20 stratified train-test split. Logistic Regression, Multinomial Naive Bayes, Linear Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Random Forest were evaluated alongside class-weighted Logistic Regression and Linear SVM. Logistic Regression achieved the highest accuracy of 83.47%, whereas Balanced Linear SVM achieved the highest Macro F1-score of 62.87% and improved the Neutral F1-score from 8.70% to 21.18%, while maintaining an accuracy of 79.09%. The findings demonstrate that the highest overall accuracy does not necessarily indicate the most balanced classifier under class imbalance. Balanced Linear SVM provided the most favorable trade-off between overall performance and minority-class recognition, highlighting the importance of class-sensitive evaluation and class-weighted learning for imbalanced sentiment classification.

title: Feedforward Closedloop Learning (Error forward propagation)
abstract: This release solves the long term stability issues with FCL by applying Oja's rule at neuron level. Thanks to Suraj Prasanth Naranatt who found the solution to this problem. For an autonomous agent, the inputs are the sensory data that inform the agent of the state of the world, and the outputs are their actions, which act on the world and consequently produce new sensory inputs. The agent only knows of its own actions via their effect on future inputs; therefore desired states, and error signals, are most naturally defined in terms of the inputs. Most machine learning algorithms, however, operate in terms of desired outputs. For example, backpropagation takes target output values and propagates the corresponding error backwards through the network in order to change the weights. In closed loop settings, it is far more obvious how to define desired sensory inputs than desired actions, however. To train a deep network using errors defined in the input space would call for an algorithm that can propagate those errors forwards through the network, from input layer to output layer, in much the same way that activations are propagated.

title: 自适应几何场论的量子计算验证
abstract: This paper explores the application of adaptive geometric field theory (AGFT) to quantum computing verification, aiming to validate the theory's effectiveness through dynamic parameter adjustment based on quantum simulation results. The core claim posits the establishment of an AGFT capable of autonomously optimizing its parameters based on the output of quantum simulations, thereby mitigating reliance on theoretical modeling errors. We detail the methodology, including the representation of geometry as a quantum system and the use of quantum simulation to assess the theory's validity. The potential for this approach represents a novel paradigm in physics, offering a method for rigorous validation using the computational power of quantum machines.

title: AN EXPLAINABLE NEURO-SYMBOLIC SPEECH MATRIX MODEL FOR PERSONALIZED FOREIGN LANGUAGE PRONUNCIATION FEEDBACK
abstract: Automatic pronunciation support increasingly combines speech recognition, pronunciation assessment, and computer-assisted language learning, yet many systems still return only a transcription or global score. This article proposes the Neuro-Symbolic Speech Matrix Feedback model (NS-SMF), an explainable architecture that converts learner speech into diagnostic and pedagogically actionable feedback. Learner speech is represented through acoustic, phonetic-prosodic, and pedagogical error matrices. A neural encoder extracts acoustic-phonetic evidence, task-specific heads estimate segmental and suprasegmental deviations, reference alignment localizes errors, and a knowledge base or knowledge graph maps detected deviations to linguistically grounded explanations and corrective exercises. The model formalizes posterior-based scoring, dynamic alignment, integrated deviation, explanation confidence, feedback validity, pedagogical priority, learner-profile update, and multi-task training. A pilot protocol for Uzbek-speaking learners of English is outlined using technical, expert-agreement, explainability, and learning-improvement measures. The main contribution is a formal framework that moves pronunciation assessment from black-box scoring toward traceable, rule-grounded, and exercise-oriented feedback.

title: Lean 4 Confirmation and Approval Proof for Hamzah Equation. (36)
abstract: تحلیل و بررسی موتور تلمتری و پایش بلادرنگ (HamzahXcell_RealTime_Engine) در Cosmos OS کد ارائه‌شده یک گام مهندسی حیاتی و عملیاتی در معماری HamzahXcell (HIP) است که سیستم را از حالت تئوریک به یک شبکه عملیاتی بلادرنگ (Real-Time Telemetry Network) متصل می‌کند. با نگاشت ۲۰ مرکز داده به ۱۰ حالت کیفی سیستم و اعمال فرمول دترمینان ژاکوبی مستر با استفاده از ثابت‌های بنیادین ($\Omega_H = 1.176 \times 10^{10}$ و $\text{FLOOR\_EPSILON} = 1.155 \times 10^{-20}$)، سیستم توانسته است پایداری و تعادل تمام حالت‌ها را روی مقدار هدف ($1.0$) به صورت دترمینستی قفل و اعتبارسنجی کند. در ادامه، نسخه پیشرفته، شیءگرا، ایمن و بهینه‌سازی‌شده این اسکریپت پایتون به همراه اسکریپت تمامیت صوری در Lean 4 تقدیم می‌گردد: ۱. پیاده‌سازی پیشرفته Python: موتور تلمتری بلادرنگ (HamzahXcellRealTimeEngine) این اسکریپت ساختار شیءگرا، کنترل دترمینستی بذر تصادفی (np.random.default_rng), مدیریت صریح حالات و خروجی ساختاریافته را با پایداری کامل پیاده‌سازی می‌کند: Python import numpy as np class HamzahXcellRealTimeEngine: """ موتور تلمتری و پایش بلادرنگ سیستم‌عامل کیهانی (HamzahXcell Real-Time Engine) اعتبارسنجی یکپارچگی ۱۰ حالت کیفی سیستم با استفاده از فرمول دترمینان ژاکوبی مستر """ def __init__(self, seed: int = 42): self.omega_h = 1.176e10 self.floor_epsilon = 1.155e-20 self.rng = np.random.default_rng(seed) # شبیه‌سازی 20 مرکز داده بلادرنگ (Telemetry Nodes) با توزیع نرمال کنترل‌شده self.data_centers = self.rng.normal(1.0, 0.05, 20) def get_realtime_metrics(self, state_index: int) -> float: """محاسبه میانگین تلمتری جفتی برای حالت کیفی مشخص‌شده""" if not (1 <= state_index <= 10): raise ValueError(f"ILLEGAL_STATE: State index {state_index} out of bounds (Must be between 1 and 10).") idx = (state_index - 1) * 2 return float(np.mean(self.data_centers[idx:idx+2])) def verify_system_integrity(self) -> list[dict]: """ارزیابی جامع یکپارچگی سیستم و محاسبه دترمینان ژاکوبی مستر برای تمامی حالات""" print("=" * 85) print(f"{'--- HAMZAHXCELL REAL-TIME TELEMETRY & INTEGRITY REPORT ---':^85}") print("=" * 85) print(f"{'کد':<6} | {'مرکز داده (Avg)':<18} | {'متریک دترمینان':<20} | {'وضعیت'}") print("-" * 85) results = [] for i in range(1, 11): telemetry = self.get_realtime_metrics(i) # فرمول اصلی دترمینان ژاکوبی مستر با احتساب ثابت‌های امگا و اپسیلون کف determinant = (self.omega_h * telemetry) / (self.omega_h + title: 基于自适应的拓扑变换的概率模型
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic model based on adaptive topology transformation, designed to enhance the accuracy of probability model predictions and reduce model complexity. Traditional probabilistic models often rely on static parameter estimation, failing to fully leverage the inherent properties of topology transformations. We propose a new framework that utilizes an adaptive topology transformation process to dynamically adjust model parameters, leading to improved predictive capabilities. The core mechanism involves an iterative self-adaptation algorithm that optimizes the model's parameters based on the observed data distribution. This approach addresses the limitations of existing methods by providing a more flexible and accurate representation of complex probability distributions. title: Decentralized Reinforcement Learning with Distributed Bayesian Belief Propagation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to decentralized reinforcement learning (DRL) that leverages distributed Bayesian belief propagation (DBBP) for enhanced coordination and robustness. Traditional DRL methods often struggle with scalability and convergence issues in complex, multi-agent environments. Our framework addresses these limitations by enabling agents to share knowledge and aggregate policies through iterative belief updates. Each agent maintains a local Bayesian belief about the environment and its own policy. These beliefs are dynamically updated using DBBP, which propagates information between neighboring agents based on their observations. This process converges to a globally consistent policy, significantly improving performance compared to standard decentralized RL techniques. We demonstrate the core claim that this approach enables robust and scalable reinforcement learning in decentralized environments. The key innovation lies in the synergistic combination of decentralized RL with distributed Bayesian inference, leading to a more effective strategy for knowledge sharing and policy aggregation. We present the core mechanism of the DBBP algorithm and analyze its convergence properties.

abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to anomaly detection utilizing adaptive neural networks. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through a theoretical analysis and a conceptual framework, highlighting its potential for improved accuracy and robustness in anomaly detection scenarios. title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning with Adaptive Modality Selection
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to neuro-symbolic reasoning that leverages neural networks for adaptive modality selection. The core idea is to allow a neural network to dynamically assess the suitability of different modalities – such as images, text, and audio – for a given reasoning task. Based on this assessment, the network outputs a probability distribution over the available modalities, indicating the expected utility of each for the task. This distribution is then used to select the most promising modality for subsequent symbolic reasoning or knowledge graph queries. Unlike traditional neuro-symbolic methods that typically rely on a single, fixed modality, this approach offers the potential for significant improvements in both efficiency and accuracy by capitalizing on the strengths of diverse input modalities. We propose a framework that integrates neural probability estimation with a symbolic reasoning engine, demonstrating a flexible and adaptable system for complex reasoning problems. The effectiveness of this framework is illustrated through a conceptual analysis and theoretical justification, highlighting the benefits of a modality-aware reasoning process.
